items.stem: A well-written AI answer states a surprising fact with total confidence. What should you do first?

options.A: Treat confidence as a reason to check the claim elsewhere
options.B: Trust it, because clear writing means the AI checked sources
options.C: Share it quickly so others can benefit from the news

items.stem: You want to verify a bold claim you just read. What is the best next move?

options.A: Read the same page two more times for hidden clues
options.B: Leave the page and look for an independent, trustworthy source
options.C: Ask the same site's chatbot to confirm its own article

items.stem: Which check best helps you judge a source?

options.A: Whether the page uses modern fonts and bright photos
options.B: Whether the article is long enough to feel complete
options.C: Who is behind the source and whether others report the same claim

items.stem: A screenshot of a headline is circulating in your chat. What does it prove?

options.A: That the headline is true and final
options.B: Only that someone shared that image, not that the claim is true
options.C: That every major outlet has already confirmed the story

items.stem: Before you forward a shocking workplace rumor, what habit should you follow?

options.A: Verify the claim first with a source you can name
options.B: Forward it with "not sure if true" so you are not responsible
options.C: Wait for three friends to react, then forward it

items.stem: An unknown blog and your city's official site disagree on a new rule. Whom do you trust first?

options.A: The blog, if its tone feels expert
options.B: Whichever page loaded faster on your phone
options.C: The official site, then any second independent report of the same fact

items.stem: Why is "it went viral" a weak reason to believe a claim?

options.A: Viral posts are always jokes, never real news
options.B: Wide sharing shows popularity, not accuracy
options.C: Only unpaid posts can be true

items.stem: A colleague says, "The AI would not make this up." What is the better reply?

options.A: Smooth AI wording is not evidence; we still need an independent check
options.B: Agree, because AI tools never invent details
options.C: Believe it only if the answer is longer than three paragraphs

items.stem: You find two trustworthy outlets reporting the same date for a policy change. What does that give you?

options.A: Proof that you can skip any future checks on related topics
options.B: A reason to ignore the original surprising post forever
options.C: Stronger support for that date than one uncredited post alone
